messages:
alex: Quick thread — can we collocate render + authz checks in the console renderer to cut the extra hop to the authz service?

jamie: Short answer: yes in theory, but tradeoffs. What latency win are you seeing?

alex: Benchmarks on a dev cluster: removing the extra auth RPC saved ~12ms p50 per panel and ~25ms p95. For dashboards with 6 panels that stacks.

taylor: Nice. But we need to think about correctness and attack surface. If renderer does authz we need strong guarantees about cache freshness, audit logs, and scoped keys.

sanjay: Also consider load amplification — authz checks on renderers will add CPU per request and remove nice separation of concerns. Under bursty traffic p99 could regress if we do heavy policy evals inline.

alex: Agreed. Proposal sketch: - renderer performs a lightweight permission check (view-level allow/deny) using a cached bitmap that is periodically synced from authz service; - for any ambiguous cases we fallback to the authz service (synchronous).

jamie: Cached bitmaps sounds promising. How do you plan to keep them fresh? TTL? streaming updates?

alex: Initial plan: push-based invalidation via authz change events + a TTL fallback. Rough config: 
```
console.render.authz.collocate: true
render.authz.cache_ttl_ms: 30000
render.authz.sync_backoff_ms: 5000
```
This keeps most checks local but lets us handle rapid changes.

taylor: Two followups: 1) What about tenant isolation for Dedicated/Private clusters? 2) Do we need additional keys in the renderer pod (KMS/HSM)?

sanjay: For tenant isolation, collocation is ok as long as the renderer runs in the same tenancy boundary and we don't leak cross-tenant bitmaps. For Private we must ensure bits are stored only in pod memory and never persisted to shared stores. KMS only needed if we use signed tokens between services.

alex: Exactly. We'll scope the feature to the right deployment classes initially (hosted + dedicated but not private-onprem until we audit).

jamie: Metrics to watch during rollout: panel_render_latency.{p50,p95,p99}, authz_cache_hit_ratio, auth_error_rate, renderer_cpu_utilization, permission_drift_alerts. Also add an SLO guard: if p99 increases >10% relative to baseline, automatic rollback.

alex: Agreed. Rollout plan: 
- feature flag behind tenant opt-in 
- 5% canary across low-risk tenants for 48h 
- watch metrics above + slow request traces + audit log sampling 
- escalate to full rollout if stable for 7 days

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: canary will be scheduled after the PR lands and CI passes.

taylor: Tests: unit for bitmap decode, fuzz test policy edge cases, e2e with authz change events to ensure invalidation path works, and a chaos test that drops events to validate TTL fallback.

alex: Security: audit team wants an extra audit log entry whenever renderer grants a view where authz-service would have denied. We'll add a sampled audit flag.

jamie: Also add an explicit circuit-breaker: if authz-service is unreachable for >10s, renderers stop making new collocated grants and route to authz-service fallback to avoid silent allow.

alex: Action items: 
- alex: draft PR with config + local bitmap cache (ETA 3d)
- taylor: test matrix and e2e scenarios (ETA 5d)
- sanjay: security review + private-deployment constraints (ETA 4d)
- jamie: telemetry dashboards + SLO alarms (ETA 2d)

ops-bot: note: please tag @oncall if canary triggers SLO rollback.

alex: OK, thanks all — will open PR now and ping for quick review.
